zh: 科英布拉大学是一所位于葡萄牙科英布拉的著名公立大学，为葡萄牙历史最悠久的大学，亦是世界上最古老的大学之一. 科英布拉大学建于1290年，是伊比利亚半岛上历史悠久的高等学府. 该校所在的古都科英布拉位于首都里斯本以北，1139-1260年曾是葡萄牙的首都. 科英布拉大学下属有八个院系：涵盖自然科学、社会科学、工程、人文、艺术与体育等多个学术领域，可授予三个学位等级：学士、硕士以及博士. 科英布拉大学同时是科英布拉集团的创建地以及创始者之一.

科英布拉大学作为世界优秀大学，曾经为葡萄牙乃至全世界培养杰出人才. 其中有史诗《卢济塔尼亚人之歌》的作者，葡萄牙公认最伟大诗人路易·德贾梅士（1524-1580年）；闰年的提出者，分角器与象限仪的发明者，欧洲宗教学界数学家天文学家克里斯托佛·克拉乌（1538-1612年）；受封为蓬巴尔侯爵的葡萄牙王国政治家，若泽一世时期的首相塞巴斯蒂昂·若泽·德卡瓦略-梅洛（1699-1782年）；《阿马罗神父的罪恶》和《马亚一家》的作者，19世纪末期优秀作家艾萨·德·克罗兹（1845-1900年）；诺贝尔生理学医学奖获得者，脑血管造影术发明者，安东尼奥·埃加斯·莫尼斯（1874-1955年）；在2007年票选最伟大的葡萄牙人中，排名第一的葡萄牙前总理安东尼奥·德·奥利维拉·萨拉查（1889-1970年）；政治音乐家乔斯·阿方索城；前澳门大学校长费利纳；澳门特别行政区第六任行政长官岑浩辉、澳门立法会前主席宋玉生以及澳门总检察长何超明等著名人物. 此外，还为巴西输送了许多教授学者. 1789年，巴西的文人志士曾要求按照科英布拉大学的模式建立一所大学，只因葡萄牙的反对，希望在殖民地兴办大学的计划终成泡影. 然而，科英布拉大学仍是巴西早期大学的楷模.
科英布拉大学于2013年被联合国教科文组织评为世界文化遗产. 截至2016年拥有约25,000名学生，并成为葡萄牙的最大的国际学生社区之一.
如今科英布拉大学列于各个知名世界大学排行榜的400所最佳大学榜单，并在QS世界大学排名中，在科研、创新、国际化、教学设备设施方面获得五星等级评价. 科英布拉大学的科学、工程、法律、环境专业进入世界最强前200名. 科英布拉大学也是葡萄牙唯一培养出诺贝尔奖得主的大学.
科英布拉大学的前身是1290年由迪尼什一世创立于里斯本的一所中世纪大学（Studium Generale），是伊比利亚半岛上历史最悠久的高等学府之一. 1290年3 月 1 日，皇家宪章发布大学成立，该校成为伊比利半岛第二古老的大学机构，教皇尼古拉斯四世也在该年认可同意：除神学院之外，所有学院都可以自由建立. 校园内的文学院、法学院、教会法学院、医学院、艺术学院自此陆续建立.
en: The University of Coimbra (UC), is a public research university in Coimbra, Portugal. Officially chartered in 1290 by King Denis and recognised in that same year by Pope Nicholas IV, it is the oldest university in Portugal and one of the oldest universities in continuous operation in the world, having begun operations in Lisbon before moving permanently to Coimbra in 1537. It had an influential role in the development of higher education in the Portuguese-speaking countries, and in their history. Due to its historic influence, architecture, unique culture and traditions, it was declared in 2013 a World Heritage Site by UNESCO.

The university is organized into eight faculties, granting bachelor's (licenciatura), master's (mestrado) and doctorate (doutoramento) degrees in nearly all major fields. It lends its name to the Coimbra Group of European research universities founded in 1985, of which it was a founding member. Enrolling over 25,000 students, more than 15% of whom are international, it is one of Portugal's most cosmopolitan universities.

Coimbra's alumni over the centuries include Portugal's national poet Luís de Camões, the mathematician Pedro Nunes, many statesmen, prime ministers and presidents of Portugal, and Nobel Prize laureate António Egaz Moniz.

The university was founded, or ratified, in 1290 by King Dinis, having begun its existence in Lisbon with the name Studium Generale (Estudo Geral). Scientiae thesaurus mirabilis, the royal charter announcing the institution of the university, was dated 1 March of that year, although efforts had been made at least since 1288 to create this first University in Portugal; it is thus the second oldest of such establishments in the Iberian Peninsula. The papal confirmation was also given in 1290 (on 9 August of that year), during the papacy of Nicholas IV. In accordance with the papal bull, all the "licit" faculties, with the exception of that of Theology, could be established. Thus the Faculties of Arts, Law, Canon Law and Medicine were the first to be created. It was, however, not to remain in Lisbon for long. In 1308, likely due to problems of emancipation from the Church (relations between the latter and the political power being somewhat strained at the time) and conflicts between the inhabitants of the city and the students, the university moved to Coimbra. This town already had old traditions in education, being home to the highly successful school of the Monastery of Santa Cruz. The university was then established on the site known as "Estudos Velhos", which corresponds roughly to the area where the Main Library now stands.

In 1338, during the reign of Afonso IV, it was once again transferred to Lisbon, from whence it returned in 1354, this time to the centre of the town which was then in full expansion. In 1377, during the reign of King Fernando, it was transferred yet again to Lisbon, where it would remain for over a century and a half. The authorization for a Faculty of Theology probably dates from this period – around 1380. In 1537, during the reign of João III (1521–1557), the university moved definitively to Coimbra, where it was installed in the Alcaçova Palace which was subsequently purchased from the royal family in 1597.
